A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NFF research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial additions and changed experimental conditions.

before.justification: v1 reports original trajectory prediction, planning, force-field visualization, and ablation results on I-PHYRE and N-body simulations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds PHYRE experiments, noise tests, planning-time measurements, and failure analyses.

M1.justification: v3 introduces a visual NFF adaptation using sparse convolutions on object masks, force and torque prediction, and mask translation/rotation to generate frames. PHYRE planning adds a pretrained TimeSFormer success classifier (Section 4.4; Appendix B.1). The state-based DeepONet and ODE pipeline already existed in v1 and remains substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds vision-based PHYRE ball-placement tasks with diverse object geometry and unseen templates. It also adds imperfect-observation scenarios through noisy N-body training trajectories and I-PHYRE states extracted from RGB images. These extend coverage beyond v1's state-based evaluations.

E2.justification: GCN joins IN and SlotFormer in the existing I-PHYRE and N-body prediction comparisons (v3 Table 1). DQN and RPIN enter the reported PHYRE planning comparison (Table 3). GPT-4o, human, and random-planning comparisons already appear in v1's appendix and are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 changes N-body central masses from fixed 5 to sampled ranges, revises cross-scenario masses and radii, replaces nine-body tests with eight- and ten-body systems, and extends evaluation horizons to 150 steps. PHYRE introduces fold-1 evaluation, 12,000 training trajectories, mask preprocessing, and AUCCESS. Noise and parallel planning-time experiments add further protocols.

E4.justification: v3 adds a DeepONet-versus-MLP ablation, noise and perception robustness tests, planning-time analysis, and NFF/SlotFormer failure cases. It removes v1's latent-dimension ablation, UMAP analysis, and dedicated SlotFormer overfitting curve. Integration-method analyses are revised; the controlled force-response analysis is retained as Figure A1 rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v3 reports prediction estimates with SEM in Table 1, replacing v1 Figure 5's median/quartile/outlier boxplots. The new timing experiment specifies three repetitions. Conversely, v1 Figure 7's explicit five-random-seed ablation disclosure is absent from v3. Existing planning uncertainty reports remain; these changes do not establish increased run counts.

E6.justification: New PHYRE results report AUCCESS of 49.22 for NFF, 36.58 for RPIN, 30.96 for DQN, and 21.04 for SlotFormer (Table 3). Noise, timing, and component-ablation results are added. N-body prediction and solver results change under revised conditions, precluding same-setting performance comparisons. Existing N-body, I-PHYRE, and GPT-4o planning tables retain their values.

T1.justification: The force-field formulation, second-order dynamics, forward/backward integration, and appendix metric definitions retain their mathematical substance. Planning equations are compressed into inline expressions. The added standard AUCCESS formula documents an evaluation metric; neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of few-shot force learning, OOD generalization, and forward/backward planning persist. v3 extends the stated contribution to vision-based physical reasoning and shifts the abstract's contrast from high-dimensional latent representations toward discrete transitions versus continuous explicit force fields.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the symbolic-input limitation with boundaries concerning varying friction/elasticity, deterministic environments, and rigid bodies. It adds explanations of NFF prediction failures and SlotFormer encoding failures. Solver interpretation changes from Euler's cross-scenario advantage to Heun3's stronger accuracy, with Euler justified through cost and stability (Appendix C).

D1.justification: Appendices A.3 and B.1 document PHYRE sampling, masks, recorded velocities, image resolution, convolutional channels, DeepONet size, solver step, learning rates, batching, and trajectory segmentation. Most existing state-based hyperparameters are retained. The new checklist promises code and data release after publication; it does not establish present availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning against static-field approaches, event-attended graph ODEs, and physics-informed methods requiring known equations, citing Kofinas, Yuan, and Chu. It also adds GCN and TimeSFormer references and removes Dohare's continual-learning citation. The broader physical-reasoning and continuous-dynamics positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much shared prose remain intact. v3 retitles the paper, updates the author block, refines terminology and explanations, shortens planning exposition, moves impact text into Discussion, reorganizes appendices, and inserts a conference checklist.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with redesigned framework and transition diagrams. Prediction boxplots and the ablation figure are replaced by tables; trajectory panels are rearranged and the force-response figure moves to the appendix. New PHYRE, robustness, timing, and failure-case displays substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation by addressing part of v1's symbolic-input limitation through documented visual modeling and imperfect-perception tests. The neural-operator ablation, planning-time measurements, and explicit failure cases better support and delimit the central claims (Section 4.5; Appendices D, E, G). These gains outweigh the loss of latent-dimension and overfitting diagnostics. Mask supervision, lost seed disclosure, and unclear PHYRE baseline training counts between Figure 5 and Table 3 still limit interpretation.
